questions.q: Why does Graham say nerds ignore fashion and morals?
a: Both shift with time and place, so they do not conform
Both are unimportant to a successful career
Both require money nerds would rather save
Both are decided by people nerds dislike
questions.why: Lesson 1 says both swing like the weather, so nerds hold on to their own values instead.

questions.q: How are good hackers more like painters than mathematicians?
a: They create their own concepts rather than follow formulas
They work slowly and polish every detail
They prefer to work alone in silence
They copy established works to learn
questions.why: Lesson 2 says coders must invent their own concepts, just as painters create original work.

questions.q: What did Graham find better than writing code on paper first?
a: Coding on the machine and fixing problems as they came
Planning every function before typing
Working with a partner who reviews each line
Studying mathematics before learning to program
questions.why: Lesson 2 says his painter's approach of fixing problems while coding worked better.

questions.q: Why does Graham say you should ship a rough prototype?
a: Feedback on something real helps you improve fastest
Investors only fund products that look unfinished
A rough product cannot be copied by rivals
Polish can be added without user input
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the fastest way to improve is to put your work in front of others.

questions.q: What does the chair analogy illustrate about software?
a: Core function matters more than early polish
Design should always come before function
Cheap products rarely succeed long-term
Comfort is impossible to measure objectively
questions.why: Lesson 3 says an ugly but comfortable chair sells, and software works the same way.
